decision_authority: PI (Adam), explicit message of 25 October 2026: use V3 for M/K; validate KIC 6267058's 16.74-day and 29.31-day signals as a separately labelled tier, planets of that system with the host undetermined; run the 11.79-day signal under V3. Later the same day: 'if those cases arrive, validate further by multiplicity (or dismiss if it comes out negative)'; the 11.79-day signal completed V3 at 17:52 UTC and passed every condition (tools/multiplicity.py).
framework: Validation by multiplicity (Lissauer et al. 2012, ApJ 750 112; Lissauer et al. 2014, ApJ 784 44; Rowe et al. 2014, ApJ 784 45), applied to TRICERATOPS FPPs as in Hord et al. 2024 (AJ 167 233). Planets orbiting a star bound to the target count as planets (Lissauer et al. 2014); the host star (target or unresolved bound companion) is not determined, so radii hold for the target.

boost.basis: Smallest published boost (K2, Christiansen et al. 2022, AJ 163 244: 5.5-70 by campaign); Kepler 25-50 (Lissauer et al. 2012) and TESS 20-54 (Guerrero et al. 2021) are larger. No KBonus-specific boost is computed; any b above about 1.6 gives both signals FPP' < 1.5%.

conditions.independence: Distinct transit events: 56 of 61, 31 of 36 and 79 of 81 event windows of the 16.74, 29.31 and 11.79-day signals overlap no other BOI. The 29.31/16.74 ratio (1.7512) lies 0.07% from 7:4, inside the 0.1% commensurability screen; with non-overlapping windows this is a near-resonance, not an alias. The 11.79-day signal is commensurate with neither (1.419, 2.485).
lissauer_rowe: not a known FP: no catalogue match (M/K frozen association; NASA Exoplanet Archive checks, literature/dated-6267058)
S/N > 10 and at least three transits
protocol: no low-order ephemeris match on another star
distinct signals: no candidate is an S/N-consistent alias of a stronger one (S/N <= 2 S/N_strong / sqrt(m n) at a commensurate m/n) or shares two or more events with it
Hill-stable system: adjacent candidates more than 2 sqrt(3) mutual Hill radii apart (Gladman 1993) with M = R^2.06 (Lissauer et al. 2011)

Rowe et al. 2014 section 5.9, checked on 25 October: S/N of the fitted transit model > 10 (> 15 below 4 days), period above 1.6 days, not V-shaped (b + sigma_b + Rp/R* <= 1); all pass (b + sigma_b + k 0.57-0.79).

mk-sap-20261019-2104058096963805696-3.label: 11.79 d
mk-sap-20261019-2104058096963805696-3.dominant_residual: Planet on an unresolved bound companion (STP ~1.9% of 2.0%); BTP and BEB below 0.1%.

caveats: G 16.2 KBonus source; Lissauer et al. (2012) report higher FP rates around faint targets and Guerrero et al. (2021) a smaller boost in crowded fields.
Host undetermined: on an unresolved bound companion the planets would be larger.
Statistical validation, not RV confirmation or a novelty claim.

Search-clock ephemeris screen: the detector clock of the 29.31-day signal (duration 0.200 d) matches DR25 TCE 7620844-2 at 1:2 (58.6216 d, the secondary eclipse of false positive K03551.01, 8.2 deg away; drift just inside one duration) and TCE 6442340-3 at 5:4 (5.2 deg). With the accepted native clock and duration there is no match (literature/ephemeris-v2/screen-6267058.json). The binary's eclipses are not evenly spaced (secondary at phase 0.458), so at most every other candidate event could coincide with them; the stars are neither close nor antipodal about the field centre; and the M/K search-clock screen is null as a population (38 low-order other-star matches against 35.3 expected over 663 signals). Recorded as chance.
